title: Tsenta vs Wobo AI, applies arrive three to four days late
summary: Tsenta vs Wobo AI in 2026: in our test, Wobo applied 3 to 4 days after we swiped. Tsenta applies from the cloud. Speed, pricing and tailoring compared.
body_markdown:
wobo applies to jobs for you. when we tested it, applications went out three to four days after we tapped apply. Wobo doesn't publish an apply time.


by the time an application like that lands in the recruiter's queue, the role has already been seen by everyone who applied the same day it was posted. you're not first, you're not last, you're applying after most. the bot is slower than you would be opening a tab yourself.


that's the headline problem. there are others.


## what Wobo AI actually is


three tiers, verified from the public pricing page:


- Free Forever: 5 jobs/day, basic matching, basic voice persona, you choose jobs.
- Unlimited: $34.99/mo. Swipe to apply (you're in control). Unlimited applications, advanced matching, advanced voice persona, you choose.
- Autopilot: $44.99/mo, marketed as most popular. Wobo finds and applies for you. Unlimited applications, deep AI matching, advanced voice persona, Wobo chooses jobs.


there's a quarterly toggle ("save more with quarterly"), but the pricing page doesn't show quarterly prices.


both paid tiers are labeled "unlimited," but as with most unlimited claims in this category, the UI ceiling is the real ceiling. and in our test, you also had to wait days for each apply to actually go through.


## where Wobo AI falls short


apply latency is the killer. in our test, you swiped today and the application went out days later. Wobo doesn't publish an apply time, so check it yourself before you rely on it. in a market where recruiters review applications in order of arrival, applying late is most of the way to not applying at all. for comparison: tsenta starts the application in the cloud when you hit apply, and in our test, Sorce applications took hours. Sorce doesn't publish an apply time either.


unintuitive UI. the dashboard sidebar has Feed, Job History, Profile, Persona, Account, plus a Tools section with Resume and Cover Letter tabs. you click around to find where the per-job customization lives.


"unlimited" is gated by the same UX-ceiling problem as sorce. every job needs a swipe (Unlimited tier) or at least a review. on top of that, in our test every application waited days in the queue. so "unlimited" is a marketing word, not a literal product capability.


the persona feature is fancy but tangential. "Wobo Persona" is voice and personality customization for cover letters. that's not the field that matters. recruiters don't read your cover letter most of the time, and when they do, voice tone isn't what gets you the interview. job-fit customization is what matters.


## where Tsenta is different


applies from the cloud, no browser needed. you click apply on a posting, the cloud runs it, and the result shows up in your tracker.


AI resume optimization is included on every tier, runs per job. the resume submitted to a senior backend posting on Greenhouse reads different from the resume submitted to a startup PM posting on Ashby. that's the customization that actually matters.


three subscription tiers, all volume-based, all include both control modes built in:


- Starter: $19/mo, 600 applications/month
- Pro: $39/mo, 1,500 applications/month
- Power: $99/mo, 4,500 applications/month


quarterly saves up to 32%, annual saves up to 36%. every tier includes AI-powered resume optimization (per job) and automated OTP filling.


$19/mo Starter gets you 600 actual applications that go out today. Wobo Unlimited at $34.99/mo gets you "unlimited" applications that, in our test, went out days later.


Wobo's autopilot tier runs in their backend, and in our test you waited days for a summary. Tsenta runs the apply in the cloud and shows the result in your tracker.


7 surfaces to apply from. web dashboard,[Android and iOS apps](https://tsenta.com/mobile) , Chrome extension, MCP for Claude and ChatGPT, iMessage bot, WhatsApp bot. Wobo runs on the web and has an iOS app.


30+ named ATS platforms, including Workday, Greenhouse, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Lever, iCIMS, Oracle Cloud, Workable, Paylocity, JazzHR, BambooHR, Jobvite, Rippling, BreezyHR, UltiPro. Wobo doesn't publish their list.

## the closer


wobo ships a real product. the team built something. they have a polished pricing page, a working swipe UI, and a tiered subscription. that's all real.


but when an application takes days to go out, as it did in our test, you're not first to apply, you're not last, you're applying after most people. the bot is slower than just opening a tab and doing it yourself.


$19 at tsenta gets you 600 apps that run from the cloud, on a resume the AI tuned for that specific posting. that's a different product.
